title: Differentiability of a Gaussian average
statement: Let $f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be measurable and satisfy $|f(z)|\le 1$ for every $z\in\mathbb R$. For every variance $v>0$, the function $m\mapsto\int_{\mathbb R}p_v(m,z)f(z)\,dz$ is continuously differentiable, where $p_v(m,z)$ is the density at $z$ of the Gaussian distribution with mean $m$ and variance $v$.
replaced: Let $v>0$ and $p_v(c,z)=(2\pi v)^{-1/2}\exp(-(z-c)^2/(2v))$. For measurable $f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ with $|f|\le1$, the function $c\mapsto\int p_v(c,z)f(z)\,dz$ is continuously differentiable on $\mathbb R$.
